blindSourceSummaries: An official country policy note on sexual orientation and gender identity and expression (June 2025): concludes that LGBT+ people in general do not face a real risk of persecution or serious harm from the state, with three stated exceptions - a socially conservative restive region, trans people, and publicly active LGBT advocacy are likely to face treatment amounting to persecution; under a 'propaganda' law, public expression promoting non-heterosexual relationships or gender transition is punishable by administrative fines or detention of up to 15 days, with repeated offences prosecutable criminally for up to four years; the 2023 'extremist' designation of an international LGBT+ movement enables further charges; notes there is no reliable information on the size or distribution of the country's LGBT+ population.

NOTE: page not retrievable at fetch time (blocked by the site's bot protection); the underlying foreign government's travel advisory for this country warns that foreign nationals found guilty of violating the 'propaganda' law may be detained for up to 15 days and deported, flags display of symbols including the rainbow flag as a crime, and advises against all travel regardless of personal characteristic, noting government support for citizens is very limited in parts of the country.

An international human-rights organisation's report (30 June 2025): courts in this country have issued 101 'extremism'-related convictions for allegedly participating in an international LGBT+ movement or displaying its symbols - approximately 98 for administrative (minor misdemeanour) offences and three for criminal liability - demonstrating authorities' determination to penalise LGBT expression, association and symbolism.
